node.statement: Actor-hull and collinearity contribution is O(tau). Using the actor coordinates and the collinearity w = v + a·(f - v) of 1.1 — so v and o sit at x = 0, w at x = -a·A = O(tau) (since a = tau/(1+tau)), f at the far negative extreme x = -A, and z as the unique positive-x extreme at x = 1 — together with the pinned top-row masses (1-tau, tau+t, -t), the positive-mass part of an admissible row can gain transverse moment beyond the O(tau) cluster {v,o,w} only by loading weight toward the extreme z. Because the range of P is fixed as span{1,x,y} (1.2), any such loading is charged against the negative-mass budget by the dual (Farkas) multipliers of the collinear pinned relation, capping the net actor-hull moment contribution at an O(tau) quantity of the form (const)·(t + a·A) = O(tau).
node.inference: farkas_dual_multipliers (collinear pinned relation + fixed range span{1,x,y})
